A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MedForget research, despite the changed title and added method. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures and tables, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Lingshu-7B unlearning experiments, reconstruction attacks and qualitative comparisons, including Tables 3 and 5 and Figure 6.

after.justification: v2 reports revised benchmark experiments, original CHIP results and component ablations, including Tables 2, 5 and 7.

M1.justification: v1 introduces a benchmark and evaluates existing methods. v2 adds CHIP: a training-free procedure combining cross-modal activations, neuron selection, sibling-differential directions, SVD aggregation and weight projection across language and vision-language layers (Section 4). This is a substantive new algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use MIMIC-CXR-derived MedForget and PMC-VQA, the same four hierarchy levels, and generation, classification and cloze tasks. Paraphrased/augmented inputs and hierarchical reconstruction scenarios are retained. CHIP and its ablations do not introduce new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The main external comparator set remains MANU, GradDiff, KL Min and NPO. v2 additionally evaluates language-only projection and zero-out pruning as explicit comparison variants within its new component study (Appendix A.7, Table 7).

E3.justification: v2 explicitly tunes methods to keep retain-set generation scores above 0.4, whereas v1's reported unlearned models operate below that threshold. It adds F/R Diff, defined as Retain minus Forget Gen Score, and controlled component experiments holding other hyperparameters fixed. These substantially change the evaluation design; the base model and 25% forget ratio remain.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's hierarchy comparisons, reconstruction attacks and qualitative cases, v2 adds component ablations across all four levels (Appendix A.7, Table 7). These test sibling subtraction, vision-language merger editing, separate modality aggregation, language-only editing and projection versus pruning, providing new evidence about selective forgetting mechanisms.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added result rows do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The main and extended results are substantially replaced. For example, MANU's Institution-level Forget/Retain Gen Scores change from 9.35/10.95 in v1 Table 3 to 41.48/47.24 in v2 Table 2. v2 adds hierarchy-specific vanilla rows, CHIP results and ablation results, and revises attack curves. Given the changed operating constraint, these are revised results rather than demonstrated same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: v2 formalizes sibling-differential directions and their SVD subspace, and Appendix A.2 adds a short orthogonal-projection derivation using an orthonormal basis Q and the operator I - QQ^T. This supplies limited mathematical justification absent from v1; the existing baseline objectives remain equivalent.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion expand the contribution from a hierarchical benchmark and diagnosis of existing methods to a benchmark plus a proposed solution. v2 adds claims that CHIP preserves sibling-shared information, achieves the highest forget-retain gap across hierarchy levels and improves reconstruction resistance.

C2.justification: v2 adds mechanism interpretations attributing selectivity to sibling contrast, modality separation and subspace projection. It removes v1's explicit limitations concerning scale, chest-radiograph coverage, synthetic institutions and single-model evaluation. New risk discussions instead address inaccurate hierarchy metadata, recovery through auxiliary information and misleading compliance conclusions (Appendices A.8-A.9).

D1.justification: v2 discloses the complete factuality-judge prompt and rubric (Table 4), identifies language layers 22-27 in Figure 5, and describes merger activation pooling. These add useful implementation information. The code/data access link remains unchanged, and comprehensive training and hardware settings are still absent.

R1.justification: v2 establishes new methodological positioning relative to LEACE and Deep Unlearning, explaining how CHIP changes the projection basis through sibling contrast and multimodal editing (Appendix A.2). Related work also adds multi-hop and knowledge-graph unlearning research while removing several general unlearning references. The positioning expands substantially beyond introducing a benchmark.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, benchmark explanations and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v1's separate benchmark-evaluation and results sections are reorganized around a new method section and consolidated experimental section; metric and pipeline explanations move partly into a substantially reorganized appendix. Citation style also changes.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the introductory and hierarchy-partition diagrams, adds the CHIP schematic and prompt/ablation tables, and reorganizes result tables by hierarchy with an F/R Diff column. The overview performance plot moves to the appendix and gains CHIP. These changes substantially revise the visual presentation beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: CHIP, controlled component ablations and the disclosed judge prompt add substantive value beyond v1's benchmark study. However, v2's headline claim of the best gap at every level conflicts with Table 2: Section-level F/R Diff is 6.56 for CHIP versus 9.99 for KL Min. Figure 7 also disagrees with the tabulated trajectories, and explicit scope limitations disappear. These gains and reporting problems affecting central conclusions prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
